cards.front: Recall a key point about Geology of Britain
cards.back: Britain's geology is remarkably diverse for its size, with rocks ranging from the Archean (Lewisian Gneiss, ~3 billion years) to recent Holocene deposits

cards.front: Recall a key point about Geology of Britain
cards.back: The Scottish Highlands contain the oldest rocks: Lewisian Gneiss (Precambrian), overlain by Torridon Sandstone and Moine Schists

cards.front: Recall a key point about Geology of Britain
cards.back: The Lake District has Ordovician and Silurian volcanic and sedimentary rocks, deformed during the Caledonian orogeny

cards.front: Recall a key point about Geology of Britain
cards.back: The Pennines are a Carboniferous limestone and millstone grit anticline, formed by the Variscan orogeny

cards.front: Recall a key point about Geology of Britain
cards.back: The Jurassic Coast (Dorset) shows a continuous Mesozoic sequence from Triassic to Cretaceous with abundant fossils

cards.front: Recall a key point about Geology of Britain
cards.back: Southern England has Cretaceous chalk (White Cliffs of Dover) overlying older rocks, gently folded into the Weald anticline

cards.back: 1. For Geology of Britain questions, use correct geological terminology and classify features precisely 2. Reference specific geological time periods and processes 3.
